Surah al-'Asr

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

﴿By the 'Asr﴾: He swore by the 'Asr prayer (the afternoon prayer), because of its excellence, as is shown by His saying (the Exalted): "And the middle prayer, the 'Asr prayer," in the codex (mushaf) of Hafsah. Another reason is that the obligation to perform it is harder, because people are busy and hurried in their trade and earnings at the end of the day, and occupied with their livelihoods. Or He swore by the late afternoon/evening ('ashiyy), just as He swore by the forenoon (duha), because of the signs of His power that are in it. Or He swore by time, because of the various kinds of wonders found in its passing. And the response to the oath (jawab al-qasam) is:
﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ That is: the whole class of mankind (jins al-insan) is in loss (khusran) with regard to their trades.

﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: for they have bought the Hereafter with this world, so they have profited and become fortunate.

﴿and enjoin one another to the truth﴾: that is, to the firmly established matter whose denial is not permissible, which is all that is good: the oneness of God (tawhid), obedience to Him, and following His books and His messengers.

﴿and enjoin one another to patience﴾: patience in refraining from acts of disobedience, or in persevering in acts of obedience, and patience in what God tests His servants with. The verb "تَواصَوْا" in both places is a past-tense verb, joined by conjunction to a past-tense verb before it.
